Engineering playbook

Owner: founder / founding engineer. Status: draft, October 2026. Applies to harrisonjrubin7-cmyk/semester. Prompts that execute it: handoff/execute/.

Three rules that never bend: RLS on every table with a test that proves it; the browser calls api.* only; student records never reach an AI provider.

1. Repository layout

PathHolds
app/Student and staff app (Vite + React + TypeScript): src/screens, src/components, src/lib, src/styles
app/src/lib/core/semester-core: pure decision logic with unit tests
supabase/migrations/Numbered SQL migrations; never edit one that has been applied
supabase/tests/RLS and policy tests (pgTAP or SQL test harness)
workflow-lab/Next.js AI workflow router and benchmark lab
docs/Architecture, design system, master catalogs, execute reports
design/Exported design-system project (reference only)
.github/workflows/CI

2. Branching and pull requests

  • main is always deployable. No direct pushes.
  • Branch per change: semester/<stream> for execute streams, fix/…, feat/… otherwise.
  • Small PRs (under ~400 changed lines where possible). Each PR states: what, why, risk, how tested, screenshots for UI, migration notes.
  • One approving review. Founder approves anything touching auth, RLS, AI gateway or billing.
  • Squash-merge; the PR title becomes the changelog line.

Secrets live in Vercel and Supabase environment settings, never in the repo. Production keys are readable only by named operators with MFA.

5. Database changes

  1. Write the migration and its RLS policies in the same PR.
  2. Add tests: own tenant allowed, other tenant denied, company roles denied on student tables, expired grant denied.
  3. Prove each test fails without its policy (red), then passes (green); note it in the PR.
  4. Backwards-compatible first (add columns, dual-write), destructive later in a separate release.
  5. Run against staging; check the read-model projection still builds.

6. Release process

StepWhoEvidence

Staging smoke test: sign-in per role, Today, registration readiness, Ask Semester block testEngineerChecklist in the release issue

No releases during a pilot's launch week, finals week, or registration opening unless fixing an S1/S2.

7. Feature flags

Every institution-visible feature ships behind a per-tenant flag with a kill switch. Flags default off in production. Remove a flag within two releases of 100% rollout.

8. Coding standards

  • TypeScript strict; no any without a comment saying why.
  • Tokens and components from the design system; no raw hex, z-index or durations.
  • Every screen handles loading, empty, error, forbidden and offline.
  • Consequential actions use preview → audit → apply → undo/request.
  • Server-side validation with Zod on every command.
  • No student data in logs, error trackers or analytics events; use internal IDs.

9. Dependencies and patching

CadenceDo
WeeklyReview Dependabot alerts; patch critical/high within 7 days
MonthlyMinor version bumps in one PR, full CI
QuarterlyMajor upgrades planned; review subprocessors and SDKs

10. Definition of done

A change is done when CI is green, tests cover the new behavior, RLS is proven for new tables, the screen passes axe and a keyboard pass, docs and the catalog row are updated, monitoring exists for new failure modes, and it's released with notes.
